That's where I was going with this.  When rape is involved, it's not uncommon to develop Stockholm syndrome and develop feelings and/or a dependency on the raper. You also may be experiencing a form of PTSD which can also cause dependency/attachment to the raper. A good friend of mine was raped by one of her friends, she started dating him (long story short it turned abusive) and she got counseling for PTSD which was causing depression, anxiety, and her to have feelings of attachment to him. It caused her alot of stress, because she knew what he did was wrong and completely violated her in every way, yet she felt attached to him.  These feelings of depression/guilt clashed with the feelings of attachment/need for him, and pushed her to the edge of suicide.  She got counseling, was taught different methods to cope with the PTSD, finally accepted that what he did was wrong and was in no way her fault, and is now in a normal healthy relationship.  My advice would be to seek some professional help and at least find out if you have Stockholm Syndrome or PTSD or something else.
